name: Craniodiaphyseal Dysplasia

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Clinical and Radiological Diagnostic Criteria for Craniodiaphyseal Dysplasia

criteria.description: Severe hyperostosis and sclerosis of craniofacial bones leading to characteristic facial deformities
Sclerosis and thickening of diaphyses of long bones evident on radiographs
Clinical or radiological evidence of cranial nerve compression due to bone overgrowth

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of craniofacial hyperostosis and diaphyseal sclerosis on imaging with compatible clinical features
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Genetic testing may support diagnosis but is not definitive; diagnosis primarily clinical and radiological

common.symptomName: Stenosis of the external auditory canal

laboratory: Normal routine blood tests; no specific biochemical markers
imaging: Radiographs showing diffuse hyperostosis and sclerosis of craniofacial bones and diaphyses of long bones
CT scan demonstrating foraminal narrowing and cranial nerve compression
MRI may show brain and nerve involvement secondary to bone overgrowth
other: Clinical diagnosis supported by characteristic facial features and radiological findings

distinguishingFeatures: Metaphyseal abnormalities rather than diaphyseal sclerosis
Generalized increased bone density including metaphyses and epiphyses
Frequent hematological abnormalities such as anemia

redFlags: Progressive cranial nerve deficits (e.g., vision or hearing loss)
Signs of increased intracranial pressure (headache, vomiting)
Severe airway obstruction due to nasal and facial bone overgrowth
references: Superti-Furga A, et al. Craniodiaphyseal dysplasia: clinical and molecular aspects. Am J Med Genet. 1996.
Orphanet: Craniodiaphyseal dysplasia. Orphanet Report Series, 2023.
